```{r libraries}
library(gpmapr)
```

```{r trait-metadata, include=FALSE}
select_api(params$api)
trait_ids <- as.integer(params$trait_ids)
ldl_id <- trait_ids[1]
hdl_id <- trait_ids[2]

lipid_traits <- traits(
  c(ldl_id, hdl_id),
  include_associations = TRUE
)
cg <- lipid_traits$coloc_groups

lipid_name_map <- stats::setNames(
  as.character(lipid_traits$traits$trait_name),
  as.character(lipid_traits$traits$id)
)
ldl_name <- unname(lipid_name_map[as.character(ldl_id)])
hdl_name <- unname(lipid_name_map[as.character(hdl_id)])
```

This vignette shows two summaries of how a pair of traits share colocalising loci in **gpmapr**: the **Pleiotropic Consistency Score (PCS)**, which measures how much the traits' loci overlap, and the **Net Directionality Score (NDS)**, which measures whether effects agree in direction at the loci they share.

We use **`r ldl_name`** (trait id `r ldl_id`) and **`r hdl_name`** (trait id `r hdl_id`) as an illustrative pair of lipid traits that share some, but not all, causal loci.

## Fetch colocalisation data

We fetch both traits in a single call and retain association statistics (`beta`, `se`) for directionality and z-score construction.

```{r fetch-data}
dim(cg)
```

## Pleiotropic consistency (PCS)

`pleiotropic_consistency_score()` measures how much two traits colocalise at the same LD blocks versus having trait-specific signals. The score is a Jaccard-style ratio:

$$\text{PCS} = \frac{n}{n + m_1 + m_2}$$

where $n$ is the number of shared loci, $m_1$ are loci unique to trait 1, and $m_2$ are loci unique to trait 2.

```{r pcs}
pcs_result <- pleiotropic_consistency_score(
  ldl_id, hdl_id,
  coloc_groups = cg
)

pcs_result
```

`r ldl_name` and `r hdl_name` share a modest fraction of colocalising loci: most signals are trait-specific.

`pcs_matrix()` extends this to all pairs when comparing more than two traits:

```{r pcs-matrix}
pcs_mat <- pcs_matrix(c(ldl_id, hdl_id), coloc_groups = cg)
pcs_mat
```

## Net directionality (NDS)

At loci where both traits colocalise, `net_directionality_score()` asks whether effect directions agree:

$$\text{NDS} = \frac{n_+ - n_-}{n_+ + n_-}$$

```{r nds}
nds_result <- net_directionality_score(
  ldl_id, hdl_id,
  coloc_groups = cg
)

nds_result
```

A positive NDS means concordant effect directions predominate at shared loci (here, slightly more concordant than discordant pairs).

`nds_matrix()` gives the same score for every pair of a larger set of traits:

```{r nds-matrix}
nds_mat <- nds_matrix(c(ldl_id, hdl_id), coloc_groups = cg)
nds_mat
```

## Session summary

```{r summary}
summary_table <- data.frame(
  metric = c(
    "PCS",
    "Shared loci (n)",
    paste0(ldl_name, "-only loci (m1)"),
    paste0(hdl_name, "-only loci (m2)"),
    "NDS"
  ),
  value = c(
    round(pcs_result$pcs, 3),
    pcs_result$n_shared,
    pcs_result$m1,
    pcs_result$m2,
    round(nds_result$nds, 3)
  ),
  row.names = NULL
)
knitr::kable(summary_table)
```
